## Triage routing

**Labels** `tests` `tooling` `finding` `domain:devx` `pm:queue` `priority:p3` · **Type** Task

**Lane — `domain:devx`.** The subject is test-harness discipline — teardown ordering and the network-escape guard — not any product surface. The two files live in `packages/app-shell`, but the gate's subject sets the lane, not the symptom's address.

**Re-measured on `83d4fda16` — confirmed. Line numbers have drifted by 2-3.**

| card says | actual today |
| --- | --- |
| `HomePage.marketplaceDisabled.test.tsx:107` / `:137` | **`:109`** stub / **`:139`** `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` |
| `HomePage.aiStudioDisabled.test.tsx:135` / `:169` | **`:137`** stub / **`:171`** `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` |

**And the load-bearing negative verifies:** grepping both files for `cleanup` returns **zero** — neither imports it, neither calls it before `vi.unstubAllGlobals()`. The same query finds `vi.unstubAllGlobals` and `vi.stubGlobal` in both files, so the pattern is live and the zero is a reading.

⚠️ **One addition the card does not carry:** each file has a **second** stub site — `marketplaceDisabled:199` and `aiStudioDisabled:263`, both `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', … status: 404 …)`. So there are four stub installations across the two files, not two. Whoever takes this must convert all four, not just `bootOn`'s.

---

## Grade p3, and the card is right that it is an observation rather than a red

⭐ **Nothing fails today, and the reason it doesn't is the reason to file it.** `HomePage` mounts `PendingDraftsBanner`, whose `usePendingDrafts` fetches only from its mount effect and issues nothing on unmount, so the window the inverted order opens is currently empty. That is **a property of today's `HomePage`, not of these files** — exactly the kind of thing that changes under someone else's PR. And there is precedent for the cost: objectui#7439 was found because it cost an unrelated PR its enqueue window.

Re-grade to **p2** the moment `HomePage` (or anything it mounts) gains an unmount-time or cleanup-triggered read — that closes the "currently empty" escape and turns this into a live flake on someone else's branch.

## The two defects are separate and both should land together

**1. Teardown order is #7439's, inverted.** Vitest runs `afterEach` hooks in **reverse registration order**, so a teardown written in a test file runs **before** the root setup's RTL `cleanup()`. Unstubbing there restores the real `fetch` while the tree is still mounted, so any read `cleanup()`'s act-flush triggers reaches a real socket. The remedy is spelled out verbatim in the guard's own `Fix:` text in `vitest.setup.network-escape-guard.ts`: *"call `cleanup()` BEFORE `vi.unstubAllGlobals()`"*. Batches 1-4 of #7307 have installed exactly that pairing in **16 files**; these two sit next door to batch 4's four and do the opposite.

**2. The stub is a sink, not a router.** `bootOn()` answers **every** URL with the runtime-config body. `HomePage` reaches at least two endpoints — `GET /api/v1/runtime/config` (what the stub is for) and `GET /api/v1/meta/_drafts` (`usePendingDrafts.ts:48`, measured in #7307 batch 4 as the escape route of the four sibling files in this directory). The `_drafts` reader parses the runtime-config body, finds no `drafts` key, and yields `[]` — inert, so nothing fails.

⭐ **Defect 2 is the one worth the card even though defect 1 has the precedent.** A sink has no record of what it was handed and no assertion that it only served what it meant to serve, so **a future new escape from `HomePage` would be silently answered instead of going red**. That is a test double that cannot fail — the same shape this repo keeps carding (#8492 / #8535 / #8410 / #8465), here in the harness rather than in a gate. The router shape #5225 settled on, and that #7307's batches use, fails on any URL outside the served set.

⛔ Do not fix defect 1 alone. Ordering without routing leaves the sink; routing without ordering leaves the socket window. The card's own summary is the acceptance criterion: *import `cleanup`, call it before `vi.unstubAllGlobals()`, and turn `bootOn`'s stub into a recording router over the two routes with an `afterEach` assertion that nothing else was requested.*

**⛔ Correctly not fixed in PR #8032.** #7307 batch 4 owns four named files and two ledger literals; **neither of these two files is on the network-escape ledger**, so touching them would be a scope breach with no gate to prove the change. ⚠️ Note the consequence for whoever claims this: there is still no gate over these two files, so the PR must carry its own evidence — the `afterEach` assertion in defect 2 is that evidence, which is another reason not to split the two halves.

**Dedup accepted and unusually well done** — the full open set updated since 2026-09-06T09:19Z read over repo-scoped REST (23 cards enumerated), on top of a full open `domain:devx` read. The two near-misses are correctly distinguished: **#7996** is an explain double answering a key no hook reads (different instance, same family); **#7439** named the ordering hazard, is **closed as completed**, and fixed exactly one file (`RecordDetailView.approvalDeclaredActions.test.tsx`). No open card covers these two files.

Triage seat only — no claim, no dispatch, no code.

⚠️ **Four stub sites, ⛔ not two** — triage's addition, and the easiest thing to miss: `marketplaceDisabled:199` and `aiStudioDisabled:263` each install a second `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', … status: 404 …)`.

⚠️ **There is no gate over these two files** — neither is on the network-escape ledger, which is why objectui#7307 batch 4 correctly did not touch them. ⇒ **the PR must carry its own evidence**, and the `afterEach` assertion is that evidence. ⭐ Another reason the two halves cannot be split.

⚠️ **Four stub sites, ⛔ not two** — `marketplaceDisabled:199` and `aiStudioDisabled:263` each install a second `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', … 404 …)`. **All four convert.**

⚠️ **No gate covers these two files** (neither is on the network-escape ledger — which is why objectui#7307 batch 4 correctly left them alone). ⇒ **the PR carries its own evidence**, and the `afterEach` assertion is it.

### Preconditions falsified against the tree first

⚠️ Anchored on **text**, ⛔ not the recorded line numbers (triage measured them already drifted 2-3): both files unstub in a locally-registered `afterEach` and **neither imports `cleanup`** — ⚠️ with a control in the same run, since that negative is the card's centre · four stub sites · `usePendingDrafts` really reads `/api/v1/meta/_drafts` from its mount effect · neither file is on the ledger · the reference router shape exists and is **named**.

### ⭐ The demonstration this dispatch will not accept a PR without

A scratch mutation adding an unexpected fetch must turn the new assertion **red**, restored afterwards with the restore proven by **blob hash** (⛔ not by an exit code). ⭐ **If the router cannot fail, it is a sink with extra steps** — which is the defect, not the fix.

## LANDED — objectui#8033 via PR objectui#8661, merged `5798df42a`

`merged_at 2026-09-08T21:17:37Z`; `merged` and `removed_from_merge_queue` share that timestamp with `merged: true` ⇒ that removal **is** the merge, ⛔ not a dequeue.

### Landing probe on a re-fetched `origin/main` (tip `5798df42a`)

⚠️ Read as **LINE ORDER**, ⛔ never presence — both `cleanup` and `vi.unstubAllGlobals` were present before this PR too, and **the order was the defect**. Comment lines excluded from the scan.

| | `marketplaceDisabled` | `aiStudioDisabled` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `vi.stubGlobal` sites | **1** (`:163`) | **1** (`:191`) |
| `cleanup()` | `:237` | `:269` |
| `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` | `:238` | `:270` |
| ⭐ **order: cleanup BEFORE unstub** | ✅ | ✅ |
| imports `cleanup` | ✅ | ✅ |
| firing control — `SERVED_ROUTES` | 2 refs | 2 refs |

Nonsense control: ✅ exit 1.

⭐ **One `vi.stubGlobal` per file is the count that matters**: there were **four** sinks across the two files, and a fix that converted only `bootOn`'s would have left two behind **while looking finished**. Four collapsed into two routers, one per file.

### What is now true that was not

**Teardown order.** Vitest runs `afterEach` hooks in **reverse registration order**, so a teardown written in the test file ran **before** the root setup's RTL `cleanup()` — restoring the real `fetch` while the tree was still mounted, so any read that `cleanup()`'s act-flush triggered reached a real socket. From `5798df42a` both files call `cleanup()` first, matching the pairing objectui#7307's batches installed in 16 files.

**The sink is gone.** `bootOn()` used to answer **every** URL with the runtime-config body. ⭐ A sink has no record of what it was handed and no assertion that it served only what it meant to — so **a future new escape from `HomePage` would have been silently answered instead of going red**. Now a recording router serves exactly `/api/v1/runtime/config` and `/api/v1/meta/_drafts`, records everything else, and an `afterEach` asserts nothing outside that set was requested.

### ⭐ The evidence, because there is still no gate over these two files

Precondition 4 came back **stronger** than the card stated: not only are these files not on the network-escape ledger — ⭐ **there is no ledger**. `KNOWN_ESCAPES` was retired when objectui#7307 reached zero, and a test now pins its **absence**. ⇒ nothing external can prove this change, which is why the PR had to carry its own proof:

- **Leg A (non-vacuity)** — demand the *recorded* set be empty ⇒ 14/14 red, each case enumerating exactly the two served routes. ⇒ the router really records, and really sees both.
- **Leg B (escape probe)** — inject an unexpected `fetch` ⇒ 14/14 red, each naming the URL. ⭐ **Under the old sink that same probe is answered `ok: true` and stays green.** ⇒ the defect reproduced and closed in one measurement.

Both proven on disk by anchor count and blob hash, restored under a trap, restoration proven by blob equality against HEAD — ⛔ not by an exit code.

### One design note kept on the record

The `afterEach` asserts **before** `cleanup()`, matching batch 4's 16-file precedent verbatim. Asserting after would additionally catch an escape raised by the act-flush — ⭐ but inventing a third shape in this family is the disease this lane keeps carding, and the root guard's own `afterEach` still runs after this file's teardown and reds any **real** socket in that window.
